summary: The article argues that Universal Basic Income (UBI) could cushion workers against job displacement caused by AI and automation. It cites expert views, pilot results, a proposed "Digital Dividend" tax funding model, and personal stories, while acknowledging concerns about inflation, work disincentives and moral implications. It closes with plans for international UBI summits, the first on September 23, 2024.
one_line: Article presents UBI as a way to cushion AI-driven job displacement, covering funding ideas, pilot results, expert opinions, criticisms and upcoming summits.
key_facts: A Thorne Institute of Technology study found that by 2025, up to 25% of jobs in developed economies may be subject to automation.
Finland and Canada have trialed UBI schemes with varying degrees of success.
UBI is defined as a fixed income granted to citizens regardless of employment status, wealth, or other income.
Dr. Lara Stephens, an economist at the Valencia International Relations Institute, said on December 28, 2023 that UBI could catalyze entrepreneurialism by providing a financial safety net.
In a January 6, 2024 interview, tech entrepreneur Vincent Rajah said UBI could help workers navigate transitions and acquire new skills without "the paralyzing fear of economic ruin."
In the UBI pilot in Utopia Springs, 15% more residents engaged in full or part-time education than the national average.
The "Digital Dividend" proposes taxing transactions or profits generated by AI, robotics and other digital services to fund UBI.
James Fuller, chief financial analyst at Digital Insights, advocated on February 22, 2024 for companies benefiting most from automation to contribute to the system funding mass benefits.
Sarah Nguyen, a former retail worker from Sovereign City laid off due to an automated checkout system, transitioned to digital design with UBI support, as broadcast on March 5, 2024.
Cultural anthropologist Dr. Michelle Yeoh said on April 2, 2024 that UBI could "liberate individuals to engage more with their communities" and foster work-life balance.
Critics question inflation, the potential deterrent to work, and the moral implications of unconditional income.
The Universal Income Project acknowledges these hurdles and urges robust planning and phased implementation.
Futurist Alexandra Knight is organizing international UBI summits, the first on September 23, 2024, to craft a global UBI strategy.
